feature: Every key dot picks on a click, Backspace deletes it
summary: A key dot on a lane, a diamond on the clip's own bar and a ring on the motion path on the canvas now each pick on a click, drawn white, and Backspace deletes what is picked while every other key stays. A shut lane follows the same rule as the open graph: click the line between two dots to pick that stretch, Command-click it to add a dot.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Type a title on a recording, key its Position, Scale, Opacity and Rotation Y at one second and again at three. Walk: every-key-dot-picks-walk.

try.do: Click the Scale dot at three seconds on its lane under the Title track, then press Backspace.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: With the title picked, click the ring where its route starts on the canvas, then press Backspace.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the line between the two Opacity dots: it picks that stretch. Command-click it: a dot is added there, picked.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Right-click the Rotation Y dot at three seconds.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the white diamond on the title's clip at one second, then press Backspace.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Shift-click two dots on different lanes, then press Backspace once, then Command-Z once.

evaluate: Can you tell at a glance which dot is picked on every lane colour, and on the clip bar?
Is a diamond on the clip picking every key at its moment what you expect, or should it pick only the clip's own summary?
On the canvas, is it right that clicking a ring leaves the playhead where it is (so the ring stays in view), while a dot on the timeline moves the playhead to it?
Does dragging a ring on the canvas to move that key's place feel like the way to reshape a route?
Does a shut lane picking a stretch between two dots, instead of drawing a box, get in your way?
rough: The walk could only land clicks with Command held: macOS would not let the probe come to the front this session, and a plain click on a window behind another app is swallowed. With nothing picked a Command-click picks exactly as a plain click does, so the walk proves the pick, the delete and the add, but the plain click itself was not driven by a walk here.

When the playhead sits on a key, that key's ring is under the layer's middle, where the 3D handles are drawn; those handles keep the press there and the ring cannot be clicked. Pick that key on its lane instead, or move the playhead off it.
A ring under the resting pointer shows the brightened hover look rather than white, so in the canvas picture the picked ring reads blue until the pointer moves away.
No mock draws a picked dot, a picked stretch on a shut lane, or a picked ring on the canvas; the white picked look is the user's rule of 2026-10-13, written as UX-PATTERNS D21.
